prompt:

Asset type: 9:16 source frame for image-to-video animation
Primary request: Create one clean mechanism-first Gradient Descent frame showing that the slope/gradient points toward higher loss and the model update moves opposite toward lower error.

Subject: friendly Indian teenage learner pointing at a large graph, secondary to the graph.
Technical visual: huge U-shaped loss curve dominates the frame. One point sits on the slope. A thin tangent or uphill cue is labeled "gradient: higher loss". A separate green downhill arrow is labeled "move opposite" and ends near "lower error". Make the causal relationship visually obvious.
Style/medium: clean mechanism-first educational illustration, simple flat shading, crisp graph, high readability, not a PPT slide.
Composition/framing: graph fills most of the frame; character is small and supportive; enough safe margin for image-to-video motion.
Text to render verbatim, exactly: "gradient: higher loss", "move opposite", "lower error".
Constraints: no lesson title; no formulas; no extra text; no logos; no watermark; labels must be large and readable; do not label the downhill arrow as the gradient.
